tasks.title: Allow returning a bike to a different dock

messages.text: Brief: riders should be able to end a rental at any dock, not only the one they started from. The operator wants to know whether a fee applies.
Plan: drop the same-dock check in the end-rental endpoint, record both dock ids on the rental, and add a fee rule if one is wanted. Question below on the fee.
No fee, but only to docks in the same city.
Thanks. One follow-up before I write the rule, since "same city" can be read two ways in our data.
Service area. The city field is just a label.
Delivered: PR #388 merged. Returns inside the rider's service area are free; outside it the endpoint refuses with a message naming the nearest allowed dock.

questions.text: Should returning to a different dock carry a fee?
Does "same city" mean the dock's city field, or inside the same service area polygon? A few docks near the river have the neighbouring city's label but sit in our area.

tasks.title: Email a receipt when a rental ends

messages.text: Brief: send a short receipt email when a rental ends: duration, distance if known, price.
Plan: queue the email from the end-rental handler through the existing mail job, template with duration, docks and price. Distance is omitted when the bike has no tracker.
Fine. Can you show me a sample of the email body when it's done?
Delivered: PR #390 merged. Sample: "Your ride: 34 min, Harbour Steps to Mill Lane, 2.40." One CI rerun on the lint job, which failed on a rule from a newer linter release than the one we test with.

events.reason: lint job: new rule from an unpinned linter release

messages.text: Brief: the fleet team wants a morning list of e-bikes below 20% battery, by dock.
The first dispatch failed before the owner started: the build cache disk on the worker was full. Cleared it and redispatched; nothing else affected.
Plan: a scheduled job at 06:00 that groups low-battery bikes by dock and posts the list to the fleet endpoint the ops dashboard reads. Proceeding.
Delivered: PR #392 merged. The list is sorted by dock with the lowest battery first.

tasks.title: Refund rides cut short by a faulty bike

messages.text: Brief: when a rider reports a fault within five minutes, refund the ride automatically.
Plan: a fault report within five minutes of unlock marks the rental refundable; the payment job refunds it and flags the bike for service. Refunds go back to the original card.
This touches payments. After the normal review, please run a second review round with the other engine before you ask me to merge.
First review fixed (refund could run twice on a retried webhook). Second round from the other engine found the refund amount ignored the unlock fee; fixed. Ready for merge approval.
Approved.
Delivered: PR #395 merged.

findings.title: Refund can run twice when the webhook is retried

dispositions.reason: Idempotency key on the refund call

findings.title: Refund amount omits the unlock fee

tasks.title: Expose free slots per dock in the public API

messages.text: Brief: partners want free slot counts per dock through the public API.
Plan: add free_slots to the dock resource, computed from live sensor counts with the cached value as a floor when a sensor is silent. Versioned as an additive field.
Delivered: PR #398 merged. CI needed one rerun of the lint job again, the same unpinned linter rule as on the receipt task.
Can you paste a sample response so I can forward it to the partner?
{"id": "dock-17", "name": "Mill Lane", "free_slots": 6, "bikes": 9}

events.reason: lint job: unpinned linter rule again

messages.text: Brief: a weekend tariff starts next Saturday; the operator will announce it on Friday.
Plan: a tariff table keyed by day type with the weekend price from the brief, applied by rental start time. I will ask for merge approval when it is ready.
Hold the merge until I say go on Friday. I don't want it live before the announcement.
Ready and green; holding for your go as asked.
Go.
Delivered: PR #401 merged.

events.text: Held for the operator's go before merge, at the operator's request

messages.text: Brief: unlocking a bike takes over two seconds at busy docks.
Plan: the endpoint waits on a synchronous lock confirmation; switch to the lock's acknowledgement message and respond once it arrives, with a timeout. Load test against the simulator.
Delivered: PR #404 merged. Median unlock time in the simulator went from 2.3 s to 0.6 s. The lint job needed a rerun once more for the same linter rule.
Brief: riders banned for damage need a way to appeal from the app.
Plan: an appeal form on the banned screen that creates a support case with the ban reason attached. No automatic unban. Proceeding.
Delivered: PR #406 merged.
Send me an example of the support case it creates?
Subject "Ban appeal: rider 4821", body with ban reason, date, rider's text and the last three rentals.
